guide_passage:
The r4 guide's passage (the passage this carries):
Close the Session and Return to Life

Give every inner-child session a definite ending. Endless processing can become another way to avoid living.

Look around and name where you are.

Feel your feet, the chair, or another external contact point.

Relax your jaw and hands.

Name one ordinary action that comes next.

Say: “That is enough for today. We are returning to the life we are building.”

The session does not have to resolve every feeling before you make food, answer a message, take a walk, or go to sleep. Returning to life is part of integration.
note: Turn 65 (2026-10-17): Simple Practices, practice 9 of 9 (Close the Session and Return to Life), for the dedup.
before: If it starts to look like something serious happened, don't confront or accuse anybody based only on what came up here. Write down what came up and how it came up. Then talk it over with someone steady who won't lead you toward an answer. And when you're done, put the photo away. If it keeps pulling you back to search it, or to be certain, stop using it for a while and get yourself regulated in the present first.

brief:
- the main point: give every session a definite ending; look around and name where you are; feel your feet, the chair or another contact point; relax your jaw and hands; name one ordinary action that comes next; say "That is enough for today. We are returning to the life we are building."; the session doesn't have to resolve every feeling before you make food, answer a message, take a walk or go to sleep.
- what the dedup leaves to add (G9): a set end to every session; the closing steps (where you are, feet or chair, jaw and hands, the next ordinary action); "returning to the life we are building"; leaving feelings unresolved.
- already in the article, so not said again: endless processing as a way to avoid living ("a ritual you have to complete before you're allowed to live"); returning to life as integration ("I'd try a tiny bit of it out here").
